A hidden step first turns two TD-DFT jobs into absorption spectra with `frog-tddft --uv --save-spectra`.
The window is 1.5–6.5 eV (190–827 nm), so the visible range is covered. Each CSV is then resampled on a
whole-nanometre grid (380–780 nm, 1 nm step) with the columns `wavelength` and `intensity`. This step is
needed because the raw `frog-tddft` CSV currently fails in `frog-cie` (see the note at the end). The
curves are normalised to 1 at their maximum, so `--spectrum-type absorption` treats each one as
absorbance 1 at its strongest band.

**Files used** (from the repository):

* `files/soc.out` — ORCA, PBE0 D4 def2-TZVPP CPCM(CHCl3), TD-DFT 1 root + triplets + SOC (S1 2.778 eV), C28H25BBrN
* `files/1_p8_orca.out` — ORCA, CAM-B3LYP D4 def2-TZVPP CPCM(hexane), TD-DFT 50 roots (S1 3.669 eV), C26H19BBrN

**1. Perceived colour of the two absorbers** under daylight (D65).

```bash
frog-cie cie/soc.csv cie/1_p8_orca.csv --spectrum-type absorption -o cie/cie_absorption.png --dpi 150
```

```text
ℹ  Processing 2 spectra with colour-science...
        CIE coordinates
╭───────────┬────────┬────────╮
│ Spectrum  │  CIE x │  CIE y │
├───────────┼────────┼────────┤
│ soc       │ 0.3909 │ 0.4619 │
│ 1_p8_orca │ 0.3127 │ 0.3290 │
╰───────────┴────────┴────────╯
✔  Saved plot: cie/cie_absorption.png
```

* `soc` (one band at 2.778 eV ≈ 446 nm, blue) removes blue light: what is transmitted is seen at
  x 0.3909, y 0.4619, in the yellow region.
* `1_p8_orca` gives x 0.3127, y 0.3290, the D65 white point itself. Its lowest band (S1 at 3.669 eV ≈
  338 nm) lies in the near UV. With the 0.3 eV default width, its tail does not reach the visible range.
  The simulated sample is colourless.

**2. Add reference points.** A small CSV with the D65 white point is written on the fly and passed with
`--external-coordinates`. Reference points are drawn as crosses.

```bash
printf 'Name,CIEx,CIEy\nD65 white,0.3127,0.3290\n' > cie/ref.csv && frog-cie cie/soc.csv cie/1_p8_orca.csv --spectrum-type absorption --external-coordinates cie/ref.csv -o cie/cie_absorption.png --dpi 150 -q
```

```text
        CIE coordinates
╭───────────┬────────┬────────╮
│ Spectrum  │  CIE x │  CIE y │
├───────────┼────────┼────────┤
│ soc       │ 0.3909 │ 0.4619 │
│ 1_p8_orca │ 0.3127 │ 0.3290 │
╰───────────┴────────┴────────╯
```

```{figure} /_static/cli/frog-cie/cie_absorption.png
:width: 70%
:alt: CIE 1931 diagram; each simulated absorber in its own sRGB colour, D65 white point as a cross.

CIE 1931 diagram; each simulated absorber in its own sRGB colour, D65 white point as a cross.
```

The `1_p8_orca` dot sits on the white-point cross. The `soc` dot is displaced towards yellow, the
complement of the blue light the compound absorbs.

**Note.** `frog-cie` should read the CSV written by `frog-tddft --save-spectra` directly (`--wl
Wavelength_nm --int <curve column>`). At the moment this fails with *No spectrum could be converted*. The
1-nm interpolation of the non-uniform wavelength grid keeps non-integer end points, and colour-science
then rejects the interval (0.9997 nm). Until this is fixed, resample the curve on whole nanometres as in
the hidden step above.
